# 3 Axial Skyrmions
- This reflection flips the sign of only one pion field, so the relative phase differs by an added π compared with refs.[3, 12, 7], where an antiSkyrmion is defined by reversing the sign of all three pion fields.  
- The convention adopted here is chosen because it provides a more natural comparison with the analogous monopole case.  
- As indicated in (3.10), the profile function vanishes at radius s/2 from the Skyrmion (or antiSkyrmion) centre, allowing the Skyrmion and antiSkyrmion to be joined continuously while setting the fields to the vacuum outside each core.  
- Beyond the simple initial conditions from the ansatz (3.7), improved initial conditions were also implemented using the rational map ansatz [11] with an axially symmetric charge n map.
